failure_summary.description: Selected a salient or lexically similar candidate instead of checking that it fit the clue’s full identifying details and relation.
Returned a semantically correct mountain name in a different, less canonical form than the expected answer.

patch.reasoning: The skill already advises checking answer granularity and clue evidence, but the agents still favored overlapping titles or nearby entities. These edits make candidate verification more operational and address literal completion of ellipsis-style clues; the alternate mountain-name form is already covered by the existing canonical-form guidance.

edits.target: - Before answering, identify the type of thing requested (for example, a person, place, object, or category) and check that the candidate fits that slot. Prefer an explicit answer attached to the same clue over adjacent retrieval noise or a plausible association; do not substitute a related entity, example, remedy, or mechanism for the requested answer.
edits.content: - Before answering, parse the requested answer slot and all identifying relations or properties, then test the candidate against the complete clue. When snippets compete, prefer factual evidence that fits those details; keyword overlap in a title or heading, prominence, or a similar name alone is not enough. Do not substitute a related entity, example, remedy, or mechanism for the requested answer.

edits.target: - Treat terse statements, quoted fragments, and incomplete phrases as information-seeking clues when appropriate. Infer the answer slot from the wording, then use the context to identify the entity or value that satisfies the clue.
edits.content: - When an ellipsis marks omitted words in a title or phrase, look for a context-supported full-phrase match and return the missing continuation. Prefer a completion that fits the whole fragment over a prominent work or entity that matches only a shorter substring.
